title: Minute by Minute
year_note: Album out 1 December 1978; the single followed on 25 April 1979.

notes.made: McDonald wrote it with Lester Abrams, and it was cut in 1978 at Warner Bros. Studios in North Hollywood with Ted Templeman producing and Donn Landee engineering. McDonald sings and plays the keyboards, Tiran Porter is on bass, Keith Knudsen on drums, Bill Payne adds synth and Bobby LaKind plays congas. It's a medium shuffle in C major with a bridge in E minor, and the last refrains move up to G.
notes.context: This was the album where the guitar band became McDonald's band: he sings lead on six of its ten songs and co-wrote most of them, and it was the last Doobies album with Jeff 'Skunk' Baxter. Minute by Minute was the best-selling album in the US for five non-consecutive weeks in spring 1979 and stayed on the Billboard 200 for 87 weeks. The title track reached 14 as the follow-up to a No. 1, and its B-side, 'Sweet Feelin'', is the album's duet with Nicolette Larson.

listen_for.note: Organ and guitar fade up together, which Cash Box singled out in its 1979 review.
Tiran Porter's bass locked with Bobby LaKind's congas, the 'bass-conga rhythm sound' Cash Box said made it identifiable.
The key steps up from C to G for the last choruses, after a bridge that slips into E minor.

leads_to.title: Minute by Minute
leads_to.why: The guitarist from Deacon Blues and Kid Charlemagne recorded it as an instrumental on Discovery and won a Grammy for Best Pop Instrumental Performance.

notes.unverified: Wikipedia's song and album pages differ on whether the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Duo, Group or Chorus was credited to the song or the album, so I left the Grammy out of this stop.

culture.title: No. 14
culture.line: Released on 25 April 1979 as the follow-up to a No. 1, it reached 14 on the Hot 100.

culture.title: Larry Carlton
culture.line: Larry Carlton's instrumental on Discovery (1987) won the Grammy for Best Pop Instrumental Performance.

culture.title: Peabo Bryson
culture.line: Peabo Bryson's 1980 version on Paradise reached 12 on the R&B chart.
